summary:
All checks pass: `python -m compileall app` clean, `pytest -q` → **476 passed**.

## What I changed in this backend repo

**Authentication (new)**
- `app/security.py` — bcrypt hashing, the password-strength rule (≥8, upper/lower/digit/special), strong password generation, JWT mint/decode, refresh-token generation/hashing. Plain passwords are never stored or logged; refresh tokens are stored only as SHA-256 digests.
- `app/models/refresh_token.py` + `users` columns `password_hash`, `is_active`, `must_change_password` (default true), `last_login_at`.
- `app/routers/auth.py` / `app/services/auth.py` / `app/repositories/auth.py` / `app/schemas/auth.py` — `POST /auth/login` (→ `accessToken` + `user{id,name,email,role,tenantId,mustChangePassword}` + httpOnly refresh cookie; wrong credentials → 401 `"Invalid email or password"`; deactivated on `users.is_active` **or** `tenant_users.status` → 403), `POST /auth/refresh` (rotating), `POST /auth/logout`, `GET /auth/me`, `POST /auth/change-password` (clears the flag, revokes other sessions). Mounted at both `/api/v1/auth/*` and `/auth/*`, because the shared contract spells the auth routes without the base path.
- `app/auth.py` — only `current_user()` changed: it now reads `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` and loads the user from the DB (role comes from the row, not the claims, so deactivation takes effect immediately). `require_roles`/`current_tenant_id` keep their shape, so no router needed touching. `Authorization` added to the CORS allowed headers; `BearerAuth` declared as an OpenAPI security scheme.

**Settings > Users**
- `CreateUserRequest.initialPassword` (optional; empty → generated), weak password → 400, `CreateUserResponse.temporaryPassword` returned once at creation only, and `POST /api/v1/settings/users/{userId}/reset-password` (TENANT_ADMIN) issuing a new temp password and revoking that user's sessions. Creating a user now also creates/links the `users` login row (same tenant+email, role label mapped to the role code) with `must_change_password=true`; deactivating in Settings flips `users.is_active` and revokes sessions.
- `app/scripts/create_admin.py` — `python -m app.scripts.create_admin --tenant … --email …` bootstraps the first TENANT_ADMIN, idempotent on tenant+email.

**Tests** — all 26 existing test files now mint a real JWT via the new `tests/conftest.auth_headers` helper instead of the X-User-Role/X-User-Id stub; new coverage for login/logout/refresh/me/change-password, 401/403 paths, create-user with and without `initialPassword`, weak password 400, and reset-password.

Reading taken: `/auth/*` served at both the bare and `/api/v1`-prefixed paths, since the contract lists them bare while everything else carries the base path.

Two items I could not do here, both blocked by the enforced path allowlist (`^app/|^src/|^tests?/|manifests`): **the Alembic migration** adding the four `users` columns and the `refresh_tokens` table (`alembic/versions/` is outside the allowlist — the ORM models define them, so tests and `create_all` work, but a real database needs that migration added before deploy), and **the CLAUDE.md update** removing the "do not build login/tokens" rule and the X-User-Role/X-User-Id security-scheme requirement. The entire FRONTEND section (auth store, http.js, useAuth, LoginPage, ProtectedRoute, change-password page, Add User/Reset Password UI, sign-out button) belongs to the separate frontend repository.
blockers: Not applied -- New Alembic migration for the users auth columns and refresh_tokens table: alembic/versions/ is outside the enforced allowed-path regex; the ORM models declare the schema but the migration must be added by someone who can write that directory
Not applied -- Update CLAUDE.md to replace the 'do not build login/tokens' rule: CLAUDE.md is outside the enforced allowed-path regex

Not applied -- All FRONTEND items (auth store, http.js Bearer/refresh-retry, useAuth hook, LoginPage, ProtectedRoute, change-password page, Add User initial-password UI and temp-password modal, Reset Password row action, Sign out in SidebarNav, frontend tests/lint): belongs to the counterpart frontend repository, which is not checked out here

endpoints.purpose: Authenticate; sets httpOnly refresh cookie and returns access token + user
Exchange the httpOnly refresh cookie for a new access token (and rotate the cookie)
Revoke the refresh token and clear the cookie (204)
Change own password (204); rotates the refresh cookie
Create a tenant user (201 + Location); returns one-time temporary password
Issue a new temporary password and revoke that user's sessions (TENANT_ADMIN)
Deactivate/reactivate/activate a user; blocks removing the last active Tenant Admin
Tenant-configured stuck-flag thresholds per stage (TENANT_ADMIN); returns a bare JSON array

context_sharing.notes: All five /auth endpoints the frontend asked for are implemented and mounted TWICE: at /api/v1/auth/* and at bare /auth/* (app/main.py includes auth.router with and without the prefix), so the frontend's unprefixed spelling works too. Auth is now Authorization: Bearer <JWT>; the X-User-Role/X-User-Id header stub is gone (those header names are still in the CORS allow-list only). POST /api/v1/settings/users/{userId}/reset-password exists. Role values on settings/users DTOs are display labels ('Tenant Admin', 'Legal Reviewer', 'Contract Owner', 'Approver', 'External Party', 'Signer'), while AuthUserResponse.role and require_roles use role CODES ('TENANT_ADMIN', ...) — do not mix them. status is one of 'Invited' | 'Active' | 'Deactivated'. GET /api/v1/tracker/bottleneck-thresholds returns a bare array, not {items}. Errors are always {error, details[]}; 401 missing/invalid token, 403 wrong role or deactivated user, 409 duplicate email or last-active-Tenant-Admin.
